content.text: Waves are all around us—from the sound of music to the light that lets us see, from ocean waves to the signals that carry our phone calls. Understanding the basic properties of waves is essential for explaining how energy and information travel through the universe.
Waves transfer energy from one place to another without transferring matter. The particles of the medium oscillate but do not travel with the wave.
is a disturbance that transfers energy from one place to another without transferring matter.
The medium itself doesn't travel with the wave
Particles oscillate (vibrate) but return to their original position
Waves on a string or rope
is the maximum displacement of a point on a wave from its rest (equilibrium) position.
Measured from the rest position to a crest (or trough)
Related to the energy carried by the wave
Unit: metres (m) for mechanical waves; various units for other wave types
is the distance between two consecutive points that are in phase (e.g., crest to crest or trough to trough).

|←── wavelength (λ) ──→|
   crest       crest       crest
    /\         /\         /\
   /  \       /  \       /  \
──/────\─────/────\─────/────\── rest
       \   /      \   /
        \ /        \ /
      trough      trough
is the number of complete waves passing a point per second.
Higher frequency = more waves per second
is the time taken for one complete wave to pass a point.
is the speed at which the wave energy travels through the medium.
Depends on the medium, not the wave source

| Property | Symbol | Unit | Description |
|----------|--------|------|-------------|
| Amplitude | A | m | Maximum displacement from rest |
| Wavelength | λ | m | Distance of one complete wave |
| Frequency | f | Hz | Waves per second |
| Period | T | s | Time for one wave |
| Wave speed | v | m/s | Speed of energy transfer |
Remember that amplitude is always measured from the rest position to the crest (or trough), not from crest to trough. The crest-to-trough distance is twice the amplitude.

AM and FM describe how information is encoded
"Waves carry matter from place to place"
— Waves transfer energy, not matter. The medium oscillates but doesn't travel with the wave.
"Amplitude is measured from crest to trough"
— Amplitude is from the rest position to a crest (or trough), not peak-to-peak.
"Wavelength is any distance on the wave"
— Wavelength is specifically between two points in phase (e.g., crest to crest).
— They're related through wave speed, but frequency is determined by the source.
— Electromagnetic waves can travel through a vacuum; mechanical waves need a medium.
